we introduce an end-to-end probabilistic framework that simultaneously learns to cluster and predict, and we show that our framework is capable of learning congruent clustering and prediction strategies.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in the absence of ground-truth clustering, the clustering task could be used to inform the prediction task and the resulting clustering strategy is not only consistent with the underlying data structure, but also more robust to the noise in the side-information.

, in addition to the conventional use of side-information, the downstream prediction task itself can serve as an additional source of side-information that can be used to improve the clustering performance.
the clustering and prediction tasks are indeed interdependent and that the two should be jointly considered in order to achieve better performance in both.
